paper_of_the_week.title: Quadriceps and hamstring tendon autografts show similar clinical outcomes but distinct strength-recovery profiles after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A meta-analysis.
paper_of_the_week.journal: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
paper_of_the_week.clinical_summary: This meta-analysis addresses Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation. The reported population was: included, with 470 participants receiving QT autografts and 466 receiving HT autografts The intervention or exposure was: Intervention or exposure not clearly extractable from the abstract. The direction and clinical magnitude of the findings are not reliably extractable.
paper_of_the_week.practitioner_takeaway: This paper provides potentially useful evidence in Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation, but the findings should be treated as preliminary. The direction and clinical magnitude of the findings are not reliably extractable. It should support rather than replace established clinical reasoning and guidelines.
paper_of_the_week.research_takeaway: Future studies should address the identified reporting and methodological limitations, particularly around effect estimates, precision, confounding, and clinical importance where applicable.
major_cautions: The abstract does not provide enough information for a complete risk-of-bias assessment.
The abstract does not clearly report statistical heterogeneity.
The abstract does not clearly report an assessment of publication bias.
Clinical importance or a minimally important difference is not clearly discussed.

specialist_takeaways.sports_performance: The study is relevant to Strength, Recovery. Sports-performance confidence is high. Transfer to competitive athletes depends on training status, intervention specificity, outcome validity, and similarity to real competition demands.
